In 17:15, guidance benefits that self, deviation bears on it, a burden cannot be transferred to another bearer, and a messenger is sent before punishment. These contacts make the focus's self-account a personal response within an informed moral procedure, not an arbitrary verdict.
findings.reader_payoff: The reader sees why the command is addressed to the person who reads: the path, its consequence, and its burden return to that bearer, after a message has first been sent.

The later verse states general limits on guidance, burden, and punishment; it does not specify which evidence is written in this book, and its messenger clause may not describe the book's internal procedure.

epistemic.reason: The channel nomination and exact context surface support the local relation. HFT coordinates and attributed roles match the supplied words, while the application of the general procedure to the personal book remains an inference.

findings.title: Reading shifts from guidance to evidence
findings.claim: The focus command to read a personal book meets the earlier recited Qur'an that guides toward an upright way and addresses enacted work; reading can therefore shift from receiving guidance to encountering evidence of what was made of it.
findings.mechanism: The focus iqra and kitab are the later reading carrier. In 17:9, recitation, guidance, an upright standard, and righteous action supply the independent trigger. Their contact changes the repeated reading act from prospective orientation to a personal review of whether guidance became action.
findings.reader_payoff: The two readings form a usable sequence: guidance is heard first, and the personal book later makes the response to it legible.
findings.containment: The Qur'an recitation in 17:9 and the personal book in 17:14 are distinct objects. Their prospective-retrospective relation is an inference; they may simply be separate acts of reading without an intended sequence.

epistemic.reason: Every HFT coordinate agrees with the inline 17:9 and focus surfaces. The phase-change interpretation is attributed and retains the alternative of unrelated reading acts.

findings.title: Self-account does not certify every self-judgment
findings.claim: The focus's self as reckoner need not mean that the person's immediate judgments are reliable: 17:11 describes a hasty human who calls for evil as for good, and the focus book can serve as a steadier record against that value inversion.
findings.mechanism: The focus's hasib carries its accounting reading and an attested supposition facet. The independent trigger in 17:11 is the haste that treats opposed good and evil as alike; when that unstable estimate meets the focus's written book, self-sufficiency becomes self-witness rather than approval of the self's own first verdict.
findings.reader_payoff: The reader can keep the force of the self's accountability without confusing it with a claim of moral infallibility.
findings.containment: 17:11 speaks generally about human haste and desire. It may describe desire rather than the competence of this addressee, and 17:14 does not explicitly call its book a correction to an earlier judgment.

epistemic.reason: The focus branch has an independent facet record and the HFT context coordinates match 17:11. The corrective relation is still an attributed inference with a live alternative.

findings.title: The account belongs to an inspectable order
findings.claim: The focus's reckoning can be read within an order of marked signs, counted years, calculation, and detailed separation, changing an undifferentiated total into an inspectable account with distinguishable entries.
findings.mechanism: The focus hasib is the accounting carrier. In 17:12, visible signs enable measurement, years are counted, al-hisab names calculation, and everything is separated in detail. Their contact makes the focus reckoning legible within a measured and differentiated order rather than as a single unexplained total.
findings.reader_payoff: The personal account becomes imaginable as something whose distinctions can be inspected, not merely announced as one balance.
findings.containment: The earlier calculation may be calendrical, and the detailed separation may describe the created order rather than the personal record's internal structure. The finding connects their inspectability without claiming that 17:12 describes a bookkeeping algorithm or that the focus today is a solar day.

epistemic.reason: The HFT trace coordinates for signs, counting, calculation, and detail match 17:12. The measured-order connection to personal accounting is attributed; the incompatible sunrise-to-sunset branch is excluded.

branch_activations.activation: Distinguishable temporal signs meet counting and detail, supplying a measured setting for the focus reckoning.
branch_activations.resulting_reading: Personal accounting can be perceived within an order whose signs and units are distinguishable.
branch_activations.boundary: The branch is unresolved independently; the role is only the HFT-attributed marker reading.

findings.title: The self is a witness within wider knowledge
findings.claim: The focus's sufficient self-witness sits within a wider sufficiency: 17:17 repeats the kafā-bi construction for the Lord, then names knowledge of servants' sins and direct sight, so the self's reckoning need not be the ultimate field of knowledge.
findings.mechanism: The focus assigns reckoning to the self. The later verse repeats the sufficiency construction with the Lord as subject and inner knowledge and sight as predicates; this syntactic contact changes the self from an autonomous final judge into a sufficient witness within divine knowledge and observation.
findings.reader_payoff: The person can be fully answerable for their own account while the surrounding knowledge remains larger than what the person can see in themselves.
findings.containment: The two sufficiency formulas may function as independent assurances, and their parallel does not prove a hierarchy. The finding keeps the self as sufficient witness and the Lord as encompassing knower in relation without making either reading displace the other.

epistemic.reason: The exact parallel construction and all HFT word/root coordinates are supplied. The nested-witness relation is an attributed inference, and the independent-formulas alternative remains live.

findings.title: The account can register direction and effort
findings.claim: The focus account can be read as responsive to the horizon a person seeks and the effort that fits it: the nearby portrait contrasts immediate desire with desire for the later life, then marks corresponding striving and its recognition.
findings.mechanism: The focus kitab and reckoner provide the place and operation of evaluation. In 17:18-19, immediate and later desire are contrasted, and the latter is paired with purposeful striving and an evaluated result. Their contact changes the imagined ledger from a flat tally of outward acts into an account that can include orientation and whether effort corresponds to its aim.
findings.reader_payoff: The reader can perceive direction and effort as meaningful alongside the fact of an action.
findings.containment: The two verses describe contrasted human paths; they do not state the internal rubric of the focus book. Intention may classify the people while the record remains an act ledger, so direction-weighting stays an attributed reading.

epistemic.reason: The exact desire, immediacy, laterness, striving, and evaluation coordinates are present. The link to how the personal book weighs deeds is an HFT inference with an explicit alternative.

findings.title: Present provision is not the verdict
findings.claim: Because 17:20 extends provision from the Lord's gift to both contrasted groups and says that gift is not barred, present receipt cannot by itself be read as the balance of the focus's personal account.
findings.mechanism: The focus carries personal reckoning. The independent trigger is 17:20's continued provision to both groups through gift that is not withheld; their contact changes a possible reading of the account from a measure inferred from current prosperity into a separate evaluation of responsibility.
findings.reader_payoff: The reader can keep worldly receipt from becoming a shortcut verdict on the person's account.
findings.containment: 17:20 also directly describes generosity and provision. The inference only says that present allocation is not a reliable proxy for the personal account; the verse does not explicitly comment on the contents of the book.

epistemic.reason: The provision, gift, and unbarred-distribution coordinates are exact. The distinction from personal verdict is an HFT inference with an alternative reading preserved.
